The whole `symbolon/` directory is correspondingly open to recensus:

- **Root Symbolon:** the seven formerly proposed root records remain useful candidates only; root identity is earned by a whole-bearing relation repeatedly needed as a source/return point.
- **Matheme:** exact native QL and Spanda work, eight determinations, `3:1/3:3`, `4+2`, torus/winding/covering, harmonics, projective/formal neighbours, Noether/Floquet/Landauer, gauge/EBM/J-space mathematical objects and operational-parity experiments belong here where their warrant is exact/formal.
- **Mytheme:** uroboros/torus/trickster, Ares/Aphrodite/Harmonia, Hephaestus, Mother/Assumption/chiasm, Apollo/Dionysus/Daphne, travelling jigsaw, **the mirror that moves first**, Neumann plates, Job's mythemic office, Taylor poems and Goethe's “Double aspects of the One” fragment can be developed richly here without inventing arguments merely to preserve their resonance. Goethe remains a light manuscript carrier and a real `/mytheme/poetry/` record.
- **Episteme:** concepts are recensed from the whole recovered field; paths/maps may gain an Objective Internality→Objective Co-Internality→Return traversal where local links cannot reconstruct it; dossiers can carry the O:I six-centre anatomy, research programmes, Baudrillard/Foucault, Noether/gauge work, hero-versus-spiritual-avatar Open research and other depth; histories, etymologies, figures and dialogues are recensed by actual operation rather than old count.

## 5. Mytheme census

Mytheme receives living images whose operation matters without making myth prove mathematics.

Required bodies after T07:

- **Ares / Aphrodite / Harmonia / Eros** — difference, attraction/relation and differentiated concurrence; neither polarity is simply good/bad.
- **Hephaestus's Net** — capture/observability/counterfeit gathering and failed surety.
- **Apollo / Dionysus / Daphne** — articulation and participatory dissolution with objectification/fusion pathologies.
- **The Prisoner** — numbering, occupied ground, administrative abstraction and refusal; political counter-image of `4+2`.
- **Antikythera as attunement instrument** — coordinates cycles it does not own for an observer it does not replace.
- **THE MIRROR THAT MOVES FIRST** — exact ratified wording; artificial/cultural reflection enters causal circulation and can move first toward source/Other before forcing the other to its image.
- **Job** — at least mythemic/psychological office, while methodological Protected Account and theological/source offices remain distinct Episteme/argument relations.
- **Mother / Assumption / chiasm** — retained where the late quilt uses the image to perform return/containment rather than prove it.
- **Uroboros / circulation images** — only where a lived image performs the recurrence that Matheme derives.
- **Travelling jigsaw / box-lid → atlas** — world-picture failure and local-chart reconstruction.
- **Neumann imagery/plates** — psychological-development imagery with source limits.
- **Goethe, “Permanence and Change”** — rich poetry home for the Two Ones/One-in-change relation; manuscript burden light unless composition earns it.
- **Taylor poetry / authored image set** — preserve wording/voice/provenance; selection later by actual argument return.

Plates may combine Matheme + Mytheme, but each plate declares which element carries proof and which makes it perceptible.

## Goethe: identity resolved, selected edition collation still Open

The admitted name “Permanence and Change” resolves to **Dauer im Wechsel**, in John Frederick Nims's translation **Permanence in Change**. The fragment “Double aspects of the One” belongs to its final stanza. It is not a second poem. Do not replace it with Eins und Alles, Selige Sehnsucht, or Faust. Preserve the canonical admitted alias/home until governing correction is recorded; a source title should use the actual edition title.

Primary publication metadata: [Poetry Foundation, August 1970 issue](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/issue/71009/august-1970) lists six Goethe poems, including Nims's Permanence in Change. Its historical index identifies volume116, August1970, p345. The [publisher's digitized poem entry](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/poems/31637/song-of-the-traveller-at-evening) explicitly names Permanence in Change and Nims, but redirects to a shared browse surface. The scan endpoint returned403, so the image was not inspected. That redirect is not proof that browse-image78 contains the complete poem.

A secondary locator, [Matthew Segall's author-hosted Goethe and Whitehead paper](https://footnotes2plato.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/goethe-and-whitehead-steps-to-a-science-of-organism-final.pdf), footnote117, attributes the final stanza to Nims in Christopher Middleton, ed., Goethe: The Collected Works, vol1, Selected Poems (Princeton University Press,1983), p169. [Google Books, Selected Poems](https://books.google.com/books/about/Selected_Poems.html?hl=en&id=LGDW6Df_y_gC&output=html_text) independently lists Nims's title at169 in the1994 reprint. The1983 first edition and1994 reprint must not be silently exchanged. Segall is a retrieval lead, not the selected primary quotation authority.

The German full poem is accessible at [LiederNet, Dauer im Wechsel](https://www.lieder.net/lieder/get_text.html?TextId=6356), with an attribution to Goethe's Werke, vollständige Ausgabe letzter Hand, BandIII, Gott und Welt. It has five eight-line stanzas. Its progression joins passing bloom, changing landscape and self, irreversible substitution and the gathering of beginning/end; the final content/form relation does not simply declare a static substance immune to change. This is a paraphrase of the encountered poem, not a new English translation. A critical/printed German witness remains to be selected and collated before exact German quotations are installed.

Proposed single selected translation house: `submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/sources/literature/goethe/goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims/SOURCE.md`, limited passage scope Dauer im Wechsel / Permanence in Change, pp168–169 (German/English facing-page locator remains a collation lead). Alternative1970 magazine house is possible if that is the edition actually verified; do not create both merely to fill one debt. Parent must decide selected object. Candidate passage `goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims-q001` remains quotation-Open until page169 is inspected. The six-word fragment above is the only reproduced poem excerpt here. Whole-poem development can proceed as a ratified Mytheme with transparent paraphrase/edition boundaries; no invented attribution to Frank or claim of print verification.

John Frederick Nims, in *Selected Poems*, ed. Christopher Middleton, vol. 1 of *Goethe: The Collected Works* (Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1983), 169. **Shortened note:** Goethe, “Permanence in Change,” 169. **Bibliography:** Goethe, Johann Wolfgang von. *Selected Poems*. Edited by Christopher Middleton. Vol. 1 of *Goethe: The Collected Works*. Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1983. Translation of “Dauer im Wechsel” by John Frederick Nims. These forms identify the selected object. They do not certify inspection of its page 169. The German-facing p 168 remains an acquisition locator. The 1994 reprint and 1970 magazine publication are different witnesses. ## Essay use and whole-poem recovery This house supplies the literary witness for the already admitted `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`, destined for `submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/poetry/goethe-permanence-change/WHOLE.md`. Its ratified alias “Permanence and Change” names the same poem; the source uses the edition's “in.” The whole is a poetic refraction of A11/A12's Two Ones and A36's return, not a formal proof of QL or an equation attributed to Goethe. The full German poem moves from blossom lost to wind, through ripening and a changing river, to changed perception, aging limbs and the passing bearer of a name. Its last movement gathers beginning and end while distinguishing the heart's content from the spirit's form. The native Mytheme must retain this embodied temporal loss and artistic return; a timeless abstraction would not carry the complete poem. The final-stanza fragment named in the harmonised quilt belongs here. No independently distinguishable Taylor utterance quoting it was recovered; ratification licenses its programme use, not an attribution of Nims's wording to Taylor. Selige Sehnsucht, Eins und Alles and Faust remain distinct works. ## Material metadata and access provenance - **Selected object:** Nims's translation in Middleton's 1983 collection. No local full copy found in the inspected repository/intake or Apple Books title metadata. - **Primary publication metadata:** [Poetry Foundation, August 1970](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/issue/71009/august-1970), volume 116; historical index identifies p 345. [Digitized entry](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/poems/31637/song-of-the-traveller-at-evening) names poem and translator; shared browse redirect and 403 image prevented page collation. - **Selected-edition locator:** [Segall, Goethe and Whitehead, footnote 117](https://footnotes2plato.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/goethe-and-whitehead-steps-to-a-science-of-organism-final.pdf) identifies 1983 p 169. This secondary lead is not primary quotation verification. - **Reprint locator:** [Google Books, 1994 Selected Poems](https://books.google.com/books/about/Selected_Poems.html?hl=en&id=LGDW6Df_y_gC&output=html_text) lists Nims at 169; no silent promotion to 1983 collation. - **German whole witness:** [Klett publisher's 2010 teaching excerpt](https://www2.klett.de/sixcms/media.php/229/350470_0239_Goethe_Dauer.pdf), one page, all 40 lines, explicitly sourced to Goethe, *Sämtliche Werke. Briefe, Tagebücher und Gespräche*, I.2, *Gedichte 1800–1832* (Deutscher Klassiker Verlag, 1988), 78–79. All 40 lines read via extracted text on 2026-09-06; image fetch 403. This is a separately identified German witness within the selected translation's verification trail, not Nims's wording. - **Identity crosscheck:** [Goethes Lyrik digital, 93052](https://goethe-lyrik.net/wissen/93052/) confirms title/incipit and WA I.1: 119. It does not establish Nims's exact translation. - **Authorial NOTES:** absent at admission; none created. Full modern translation is neither copied nor stored here. ## Passages and excerpts ## Passage card — `goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims-q001` — final-stanza translation lead > Double aspects of the One - **Locator:** selected 1983 edition, p 169, final stanza; quoted fragment independently located in Segall's quotation, footnote 117. - **Status:** Open — selected-edition quotation not collated. - **Verification:** exact six-word retrieval lead checked 2026-09-06; no claim of primary print transcription. - **Source relation:** resonant with the native Two Ones; excerpt lead only for Nims wording. - **Evidential action:** identifies the fragment and blocks a second-poem substitution. - **Consumers:** `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`; A11; A12; A36. - **Use boundary:** do not publish as verified 1983 quotation until p 169 is inspected. Capitalized One in translation is not proof that Goethe taught QL's two differentiated ones. ## Passage card — `goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims-q002` — German content and form > Den Gehalt in deinem Busen / Und die Form in deinem Geist. - **Locator:** Dauer im Wechsel, lines 39–40; Klett 2010 single-page excerpt from FA I.2: 78–79. Slash denotes the printed line break. - **Status:** German digital-witness wording-verified; selected 1983 translation quotation remains Open. - **Verification:** transcribed from the complete line-numbered Klett extracted text 2026-09-06; not image-collated and not checked in the 1988 printed volume. - **Source relation:** extracted from the explicitly named German witness; resonant with the essay's whole-bearing return. - **Evidential action:** supports the actual closing distinction; qualifies a flattened static-One reading. - **Consumers:** `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`; A12; A36. - **Use boundary:** this German wording does not authorize an invented Nims English translation. Native QL standing survives the translation debt. ## Open source tasks Inspect selected 1983 p 169; verify bibliographic title/imprint against that object; collate the short Nims excerpt. Compare German-facing text if used. Resolve the magazine scan only if 1970 becomes a specifically named comparison witness. Citation/quotation axes remain independent of the admitted Mytheme's Argued operation.
